Issue details

September 2026

Remote Desktop Services might become unstable
StatusOriginating updateHistory
MitigatedOS Build 26200.9445
KB5999008
2026-09-08		Last updated: 2026-09-12, 14:20 PT
Opened: 2026-09-10, 09:12 PT

After installing the September 2026 Windows security update (KB5999008), released September 8, 2026, some organizations might experience issues with Remote Desktop Services (RDS). In some environments, RDS might become unstable, resulting in RDP connections failing after several minutes, sign-in issues, or servers hanging at "Please wait for the Remote Desktop Configuration".

Workaround: This issue is mitigated using a Known Issue Rollback (KIR). Enterprise-managed devices can resolve this issue by installing and configuring the special Group Policy linked below.

Affected platforms:

  • Client: Windows 11, version 25H2; Windows 11, version 24H2
  • Server: Windows Server 2025

Next steps: We are working on a resolution and will provide more information when it is available.

Credential Guard protected machine accounts might lose secure channel
StatusOriginating updateHistory
ConfirmedOS Build 26200.9445
KB5999008
2026-09-08		Last updated: 2026-09-10, 10:00 PT
Opened: 2026-09-09, 16:40 PT

After installing the September 8, 2026, Windows security update (KB5999008), some Credential Guard protected machine accounts might lose their secure channel with an on-premises Active Directory (AD) domain. Users might be unable to sign in interactively with valid domain credentials. This issue is more likely on devices where Kerberos authentication uses machine account password rotation.

Affected platforms:

  • Client: Windows 11, version 25H2; Windows 11, version 24H2
  • Server: None

Next steps: We are investigating and will provide an update when more information is available.

Some USB audio devices might fail to start
StatusOriginating updateHistory
Resolved KB5999020OS Build 26200.9278
KB5999001
2026-08-27		Resolved: 2026-09-14, 10:00 PT
Opened: 2026-08-29, 11:02 PT

After installing KB5999001, some USB Audio Class 1.0 devices might fail to start. The device displays "This device cannot start (Code 10)."

Resolution: This issue was resolved by the out-of-band update KB5999020, released September 14, 2026, and in updates released after this date.

Affected platforms:

  • Client: Windows 11, version 25H2; Windows 11, version 24H2
  • Server: Windows Server 2025
